newsitem.title: UK: Westminster to expand assisted care sixfold.
newsitem.headline: Westminster to expand assisted care sixfold.

text.p: British nursing home and care group Westminster Health Care Holdings Plc said on Wednesday it planned to increase the number of assisted living apartments on its books more than six-fold over the next five years to around 1,000.

Westminster earlier announced the acquisition of PPP Beaumont Plc, a company which specialises in nursing homes and in building specialised housing for older people offering access to high levels of nursing and practical care, a concept imported from the U.S.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, Westminster's chief executive Pat Carter said "We don't want to rush at it but we can start building it up. We would like to have 1000 units over the next five years."
Westminster paid 22.6 million stg to PPP health Care Group Plc for the Beaumont business, which comprised nine existing nursing homes, two under construction and 148 special apartments.

Carter said assisted living was somewhere between sheltered housing projects, where elderly people have the services of a warden, and moving into a nursing home. He said it offered people the chance to settle in one place, knowing they could receive high-level nursing care and services such as meals and cleaning if their health deteriorated.
"People who are independent know they are going to age and want to move somewhere they can still live independently," said Carter.

The 148 existing Beaumont apartments are all on nursing home sites. "We have got a number of sites which have been developed on nursing homes...we feel we could add to these existing developments," he said.

Carter said the concept was targeted at wealthier individuals with existing apartments in prosperous areas such as Chorleywood in south-east England, Prestbury near Manchester and Edgbaston in Birmingham.
Under the agreement announced on Wednesday PPP, which is Britain's largest provider of long-term healthcare insurance, will work closely with Westminster in developing services for the elderly.
Carter said he would announce further acquisitions in health care "in the next few months," adding "we are always looking at things."
Last year Westminster launched a failed bid for its British rival Goldsborough Healthcare Plc, in which it continues to hold a nine percent stake.

Carter said Westminster was taking a "wait and see" approach on whether to sell or retain its stake. "We are keeping that under review. We are looking to see them add value to our stake," he told Reuters.

Carter said he did not expect Britain's newly-elected Labour government to alter the growing market for private care and said the government seemed to support a mixture of private and public provision.
